title: [.NET] GodotObject.HasConnections(StringName) always returns true
body:
### Tested versions

Reproduced in 4.4.1-mono
Reproduced in 4.5.1-mono
Reproduced in 4.6-dev4-mono

### System information

Godot v4.4.1.stable.mono - Ubuntu 25.10 25.10 on Wayland - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Mobile) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1070 (nvidia; 580.95.05) - AMD Ryzen 9 7900X 12-Core Processor (24 threads)

### Issue description

A signal defined in a C# will always have a connection on it whose callable is `Node(<script>)::EventSignalMiddleman::<SignalName>`. That signal is returned in the signal list when getting all connections, and `GodotObject.HasConnections()` return value of true seems to stem from this.

This appears to come from https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/235a32ad11f40ecba26d6d9ceea8ab245c13adb0/modules/mono/signal_awaiter_utils.cpp#L75.

I expect Godot's always-on under-the-hood helpers to not interfere with game logic. This middleman renders `HasConnections()` useless for any C#-defined signal. If I'm correct that this connection can't be removed (or would break key engine features if it were) then I don't think it should be returned _at all_ when listing connections to a script caller, and shouldn't be factored into the result of a script calling `HasConnections()`.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a C# script for a Node and define any custom signal in that script.
2. Define `_Ready()` to print return values of `HasConnections(<signal_name>)` and `GetSignalConnectionsList(<SignalName>)`.
3. Run a scene with that script.

Included MRP contains a single scene and script you can run to observe this behavior.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[signal_connection_repro.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/23700002/signal_connection_repro.zip)
